- **self**: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing (17/6)

## Definitions

- [statement] User needs are one framing input alongside organizational and wider-system constraints. GOV.UK includes policy intent and operational constraints; Joffres argues that good design moves between user, strategic, planetary and societal needs. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://marvelapp.com/blog/design-thinking-isnt-the-problem-human-centered-design/

## How it works

- [statement] A process diagram alone is insufficient preparation for complex framing work. Joffres calls design processes scaffolding and emphasizes practitioner abilities; van der Bijl-Brouwer concludes that framing complex societal problems requires a sophisticated skillset and expertise. (medium confidence) — https://marvelapp.com/blog/design-thinking-isnt-the-problem-human-centered-design/ · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405872618301114

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Treat lifecycle phases as revisitable activities rather than a one-way approval sequence: the Design Council says learning can return teams to earlier work, and van der Bijl-Brouwer’s public and social innovation study found nonlinear co-evolution of problem frames and solution spaces. (medium confidence) — https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/our-resources/the-double-diamond/ · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405872618301114
- [statement] In their survey of practitioners’ client innovation projects, Dell’Era and colleagues report that reframing practices were positively associated with innovation radicalness whereas framing practices were not. They explicitly state that their cross-sectional data limit causal inference over time; this is contextual evidence rather than proof that a lifecycle guarantees innovation. (low confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0148296326002559 · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing
- [statement] Human-centered design starts from understanding the people affected by a problem; IDEO U describes involving stakeholders throughout the process rather than only at its beginning or end. (medium confidence) — https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/our-resources/the-double-diamond/ · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://www.ideou.com/blogs/inspiration/what-is-human-centered-design?srsltid=AYCX9vKFS7wpqGtEIHQ-ADifYB5mUqj0FGMs5ntRc0yv06O8XicRYcJ8
- [statement] For assumptions, GOV.UK distinguishes hard constraints from processes that can change and uses constraints to prioritize risky assumptions for alpha. IDEO U likewise advises remaining receptive to being wrong rather than treating assumptions as settled knowledge. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://www.ideou.com/blogs/inspiration/what-is-human-centered-design?srsltid=AYCX9vKFS7wpqGtEIHQ-ADifYB5mUqj0FGMs5ntRc0yv06O8XicRYcJ8

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Design Council names its Double Diamond activities Discover, Define, Develop and Deliver: understand the problem, use discovery insights to reframe it, explore alternative answers, and test small-scale solutions to reject or improve them. (low confidence) — https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/our-resources/the-double-diamond/ · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing
- [statement] Frame an assigned solution as a problem before committing to it. Interrogate the brief, break down assumptions, and keep the initial problem statement open to revision through contact with people affected by it. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://uxdesign.cc/how-to-properly-frame-your-design-challenge-eccb4d89cb83
- [statement] A useful framing exercise states the intended impact, records context and constraints, and revisits the question as understanding develops; scope also needs an explicit agreement about what falls outside the problem. (medium confidence) — https://uxdesign.cc/how-to-properly-frame-your-design-challenge-eccb4d89cb83 · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works
- [statement] In GOV.UK’s delivery model, discovery ends with a decision whether to enter alpha. The decision considers whether a viable service would help users and whether pursuing it is cost effective; stopping after discovery can be the appropriate outcome. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing
- [statement] GOV.UK recommends identifying hard and soft constraints during discovery. If work continues, dependencies that could make the service unviable should inform which risky assumptions receive attention during alpha. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing
- [statement] GOV.UK’s transition to alpha calls for an understanding of the wider problem context, ideas to test and their initial priority, a rough team plan, and a plan for measuring success. These provide concrete readiness criteria for that transition. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing
- [statement] Problem framing should allow alternatives to building the initially proposed service: GOV.UK explicitly lists content, campaigns, partnerships and better advice as possible responses, while Kal Joffres describes a project whose learning changed its initial app-education brief toward behaviour change. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://marvelapp.com/blog/design-thinking-isnt-the-problem-human-centered-design/
- [statement] IDEO U presents Inspiration, Ideation and Implementation as overlapping phases; its account covers learning from people, translating insights into opportunities through early prototypes, and refining concepts with implementation planning. These are IDEO U’s phase labels. (low confidence) — https://www.ideou.com/blogs/inspiration/what-is-human-centered-design?srsltid=AYCX9vKFS7wpqGtEIHQ-ADifYB5mUqj0FGMs5ntRc0yv06O8XicRYcJ8 · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing
- [statement] Treat the lifecycle as iterative: learning can change the problem frame and send a team back to earlier work. Design Council allows making and testing early ideas during discovery; IDEO U explicitly says its phases are not always linear. (medium confidence) — https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/our-resources/the-double-diamond/ · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://www.ideou.com/blogs/inspiration/what-is-human-centered-design?srsltid=AYCX9vKFS7wpqGtEIHQ-ADifYB5mUqj0FGMs5ntRc0yv06O8XicRYcJ8
- [statement] GOV.UK discovery guidance says to interrogate a prescribed solution, reframe it as a problem, break down assumptions and agree what falls outside the problem. Its example replaces a requirement to build an interactive map with the goal of helping people find their nearest contact centre. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing
- [statement] GOV.UK discovery guidance cautions against starting to build the service during discovery and says research may identify alternatives to building a service at all. Scope that advice to service construction: Design Council separately allows early idea-making and testing within discovery. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works · keywords: Human-centered design lifecycle and problem framing · also: https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/our-resources/the-double-diamond/
